proposal.summary: Layer has no adopted winner (layers.json: winners=[], decision="research", current_choice="Mover early-entry studies v1 and v2 found no development pass; Mover v3 core is preregistered and not frozen."). In-repo evidence, verified by reading the actual files: v1 ran 768 rule-exits and v2 ran 244 more (families E/F/P) on a frozen, cost-aware preregistered split -- 0/1012 pass net of costs (blueprints/us-equities/mover-early-entry/README.md; evidence/summary-dev-val-run-v1.json sha256 9d8c3d5b...; evidence/summary-v2-dev-val-run-v1.json sha256 75a5004b...). This falsifies naive long-only "detect an extreme mover, ride it" rules on this stack, and v3's own core draft (protocol-core-draft.json, status draft_pending_independent_pre_outcome_review, frozen_before_outcomes:false) is built on a literature-verified reversal/lottery-demand prior (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw MAX effect), not a continuation prior. A separate, already-adversarially-verified sweep two days before this pass (catalogs/us-equities/mover-v3-sweep-20260924.json, 23 items) covers execution (Alpaca trailing_stop/OCO), halt/LULD data (databento/dbn normalized status schema) and several literature priors (days-to-cover, overnight/intraday tug-of-war) -- I cross-checked it and found no name overlap with this task's 15 candidates, so this pass is genuinely additive, not duplicative, with two exceptions folded into "rejected" below. No candidate anywhere meets the full compound requirement (detect+auto-size+auto-exit, preregistration-ready, US equities) as one system; the only full-shape system found is crypto/Bybit-scoped and off-requirement. The task's own adversarial-verification block was truncated after "kronos-repo-license-date"; I independently supplemented the gap via gh api / pypi.org / WebSearch / WebFetch (Kelly-Criterion, itch-book, Crypto Pump Scanner, Kronos re-check, the VPIN flash-crash controversy, and a direct re-fetch of the TLM abstract) rather than treating unverified claims as verified -- these are marked below. Per repo policy (docs/paper-lane-policy.md; AGENTS.md: "Paper orders go only through the deterministic adaptive-paper engine; models stay in research"), none of these candidates can move a paper-lane number directly regardless of merit -- their entire effect is on whether a future v3-successor ever earns a freeze/promotion.

challengers.name: NoEdge-Bench (permutation-null / leak audit)
challengers.why_better: No component anywhere in this repo audits the mover-early-entry pipeline itself for look-ahead leakage or noise-fit. v1/v2's own 0/1012 result has never been checked against a permutation-null control, and v3's H1/H3 literature priors will need the same gate before any future 'survives' claim is trusted. NoEdge-Bench's own README demonstrates exactly this failure mode: a centered moving-average feature that peeked one step ahead scored AUC 0.74, and collapsed to 0.50 (null) once made strictly causal.
challengers.trial_plan: Install nexusfinancial-dev/noedge-bench at tag v1.0.0 (MIT, released 2026-08-07) into a disposable venv. Apply its permutation-null methodology to the already-frozen v1 split (protocol.json, frozen 4e57667a) using the existing 704-qualifying-rule-exit development set (evidence/summary-dev-val-run-v1.json). Pass criterion: the real (non-shuffled) v1 result must be statistically indistinguishable from its own permutation-null distribution (matching NoEdge-Bench's own p=0.83 example) -- this would confirm the 0/768 finding is leak-free, not a bug. Overturn condition: if the real result IS distinguishable from the null in a way summarize.py did not surface, that reopens whether 'no pass' hides a leak-driven false negative, and any future v3 pass claim must clear the same gate before being reported as a result.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none: a research-integrity audit of the offline preregistered pipeline, not a signal or order path; gates whether a future v3 pass is ever trusted enough to be proposed for promotion.

challengers.name: LPPLS (reframed as reversal/exit-timing overlay)
challengers.why_better: The candidate list framed LPPLS as an early-entry/'ride the blow-off' tool, but Sornette's estimator targets the critical time t_c of a bubble's regime change -- a reversal signal, which is exactly this repo's own already-verified prior (Bali-Cakici-Whitelaw MAX/lottery-reversal effect, 'survives' in mover-v3-sweep-20260924.json) rather than a continuation signal the repo's v1/v2 already falsified twice (0/768, 0/244). Merit lies in testing it as an exit/reversal overlay on movers the repo already selects, not as a new entry trigger.
challengers.trial_plan: pip install lppls==0.6.24 (PyPI, MIT, pinned to commit 69bcd7d / 2026-05-30) into a disposable venv. Reuse already-collected v1 candidate/intraday bars (mover-early-entry/collect.py output, D2) for the movers already labelled >=100%/>=200% in evidence/summary-dev-val-run-v1.json -- no new acquisition. Fit LPPLS.fit on each pre-peak window and compare estimated t_c against the mover's already-recorded actual local-top timestamp. Pass criterion: t_c error must beat a naive 'reversal N minutes after threshold' baseline at v1's own bootstrap standard. Overturn condition: no improvement over naive, or unstable/non-convergent fits on this repo's short intraday windows (LPPLS is normally fit on longer daily histories) -- drop rather than deploy.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none: stays in the research/preregistration track; earliest possible effect is a future v3-successor freeze proposal.

challengers.name: Wiseek Filing Impact dataset
challengers.why_better: This repo has native EdgarTools SEC access (data-edgartools winner) but no filing-importance-to-price-reaction dataset, and no other candidate touches the 'catalyst/news' category with an open, reproducible per-event dataset rather than a paid live-feed API. CC-BY-4.0, per-event file (events_score7plus.csv, 13,760 filings) with a stated reproduction recipe and checksums.
challengers.trial_plan: Clone WiseekAI/wiseek-datasets read-only (pushed 2026-09-12). For tickers/accessions this repo's own EdgarTools path can also retrieve, independently re-derive Wiseek's 'excess next-session move' using this repo's own session/price semantics (exchange_calendars-based) instead of trusting Wiseek's number as-is. Pass criterion: independently-computed excess-move series agree with Wiseek's within a small tolerance on the overlapping sample. Overturn condition: material disagreement, or the proprietary score cannot be reproduced without the undisclosed model -- caps this at a hypothesis-generation source, not a tradeable feature.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none: gated by the same preregistration and cost/PIT discipline as the rest of mover-v3.

challengers.name: exitkit (additional exit-policy arm)
challengers.why_better: v1/v2 already ran 1,012 rule-exit combinations through in-house rules.py with zero passes; exitkit's 27 independently-authored exit policies (stop-loss/take-profit/time/volatility/signal-reversal/convergence) are the cheapest way to widen that search rather than hand-writing more rules. Already flagged as a 'lead' in this repo's own architecture/trading.json (2026-09-19, not_adopted, 'source/tests and hypothesis selection bias not examined') for the adjacent execution/risk layer -- this pass converges with, not duplicates, that signal.
challengers.trial_plan: pip install exitkit==0.1.0 (PyPI, MIT, only release, 2026-09-03) into a disposable venv. Wire its backtesting.py adapter as one more arm on the SAME frozen v1 development split (protocol.json). Pass criterion: identical to v1's own bar -- >=200 development trades, positive mean net return, holds on the untouched validation split. Overturn condition: given the 0/1012 prior, any apparent pass must additionally clear the NoEdge-Bench permutation-null gate above before being reported as real, not noise (v1 already saw 16/704 positive pre-cost by chance).
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none: exits that reach the paper engine already go through Alpaca's own trailing_stop/OCO broker-held order classes per the 2026-09-24 mover-v3 sweep's execution decision, not a hand-rolled library -- exitkit stays strictly in offline research.

challengers.name: riskkit (sizing / drawdown / pre-trade-validator arm)
challengers.why_better: v1/v2 held a single fixed preregistered auto-leverage schedule and never searched sizing at all. riskkit's PositionSizer/DrawdownManager/CorrelationGuard/PreTradeValidator (zero runtime deps, MIT, pushed 2026-07-02) adds sizing as a second, orthogonal search dimension cheaply; also already an existing 'lead' in architecture/trading.json.
challengers.trial_plan: pip install riskkit-quant==0.4.2 (PyPI name differs from repo name; exact GitHub-tag match) into a disposable venv. Fix the best-so-far (still-failing) exit rule from the exitkit trial and vary only riskkit's sizing/drawdown parameters on the same split, same permutation-null gate. Pass/overturn criteria identical in structure to exitkit's.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none: leverage/sizing that reaches the paper engine is the deterministic adaptive-paper engine's own code path, not a research-side library.

challengers.name: orderflow-metrics (OFI / Kyle's lambda / trade-sign)
challengers.why_better: Neither v1/v2 (daily/session rules) nor v3's H1/H3 (daily-close literature priors) test the layer's named 'order-flow' or 'momentum-ignition' categories at all -- the two genuinely open sub-requirements. This is the only candidate with working, README-confirmed OFI, Kyle's lambda, Lee-Ready trade-sign classification, information-driven bars and LOB reconstruction in one place, actively released days before this check. Its true latest is npm/tag v0.52.0 (29 tags since 2026-07-28); the PyPI mirror is stale at v0.40.0 -- adopt from npm/GitHub, not PyPI.
challengers.trial_plan: Do not add a Node runtime dependency for a handful of closed-form formulas: port bucketByVolume/vpin, kyleLambda, tickRule/leeReady and depth-imbalance to pure Python, checked line-for-line against the TypeScript source (pin the exact tag) and its own README worked examples as fixtures. Feed it BBO/trade data from the itch-book substrate (or a short Alpaca SIP sample, already covered by the data-alpaca-py winner) for movers v1/v2 already flagged; test whether a pre-threshold OFI/Kyle's-lambda spike predicts the eventual move's sign/magnitude better than a no-signal null, on held-out movers, at the pipeline's existing bootstrap standard. Overturn condition: no separation from null, or the signal disappears once realistic costs/latency are added.
challengers.paper_lane_impact: none: a new, untested signal family that would need its own preregistration before touching engines-run/paper-acts-passed/paper-fills.

challengers.name: itch-book (order-by-order data substrate)
challengers.why_better: The order-flow trial above needs real microstructure, not synthetic bars. itch-book parses actual NASDAQ TotalView-ITCH 5.0 into BBO/trades/order-by-order/depth Parquet, MIT, and I independently reconfirmed it today (2026-09-26) even fresher than claimed: gh api shows pushed_at 2026-09-21 (vs. the candidate's stated 2026-09-06), tag v0.2.1 matching PyPI (4 releases). It is infrastructure, not a signal, so it earns a place only alongside the orderflow-metrics trial.
challengers.trial_plan: pip install itch-book==0.2.1 against a small, legitimately-licensed ITCH sample (this repo's Alpaca/SIP entitlement does not include raw ITCH -- a licensing gap to close first, consistent with the market-data-reference layer's open licensing gaps). Cross-check derived BBO/trade prints against the same symbol/window's Alpaca bars for basic provenance (price levels, timing) before using it for any feature. Note: the 2026-09-24 mover-v3 sweep already chose Databento's normalized status schema over raw ITCH H/h/J messages specifically for halt/LULD reconstruction -- itch-book's fit is the lit order-book side, not the halt-resumption side, which already has its own newer decision.

challengers.name: ClusterLOB (order-flow clustering, stretch item)
challengers.why_better: The only dated, primary-sourced academic method found anywhere in this search that is methodologically adjacent to 'momentum-ignition' via participant-cluster order-flow-imbalance signals reported to beat non-clustered benchmarks (K-means++ on one year of NASDAQ MBO data). No author code exists and it does not overlap anything in mover-v3-sweep-20260924.json or the architecture catalogs, so it is a genuinely new, but high-effort, addition.
challengers.trial_plan: Deferred/stretch: requires an original from-scratch implementation (K-means++ clustering of MBO data into 3 clusters, 30-minute-bucket per-cluster OFI) on the same itch-book/Databento MBO substrate, evaluated with the same permutation-null and cost discipline as the rest of this set. Take on only after the cheaper orderflow-metrics/itch-book trial either succeeds or motivates a clustering refinement.

Monitors 500+ pairs every 3s, auto-trades volume spikes with TP cascade.' Crypto/Bybit market structure (no LULD bands, no regulatory halts, continuous session) does not transfer to US equities without a rebuild. Kept only as an architectural-pattern reference (detect+auto-entry+staged-exit in one system), not an adoptable component.

rejected.name: VPIN / Flow Toxicity (Easley, Lopez de Prado, O'Hara, SSRN 1695041)
rejected.reason: Metadata only, and independently reconfirmed via WebSearch to be a genuinely contested, 15-year-old finding: Andersen & Bondarenko, 'VPIN and the Flash Crash' (SSRN 1881731) and related work report VPIN peaked after, not before, the 2010 crash and is a poor short-run volatility predictor once trading intensity is controlled for, against a published rejoinder from the original authors. Not a standalone challenger; retained only as the theoretical grounding already implemented inside the orderflow-metrics challenger above.

rejected.name: TLM: Trajectory-Aware Retrieval Agents (arXiv:2607.21625)
rejected.reason: Metadata only even after a direct read: I independently re-fetched the abstract today. It confirms 'earnings call surprise prediction, and overnight stock gap prediction' as two of three evaluated tasks and states TLM 'yields consistent, economically meaningful gains on the two financial tasks,' but names no dataset, split, or performance number for either -- nothing concrete to build a falsifiable trial against. A general temporal-decision-making architecture paper (title/authors confirmed: Wang, Shen, Niu), not an equities-specific demonstrated result.

rejected.name: "Pausing the Panic?" KOSPI circuit-breaker study (SSRN 7208358)
rejected.reason: Off-requirement as a direct result (Korean KOSPI, not US LULD) and not a new gap: catalogs/us-equities/mover-v3-sweep-20260924.json already registered and deferred the halt/LULD-reconstruction item (repository_decisions/mover-v3-dbn-status-schema, Databento normalized status schema, contested) two days before this pass. Better attached to that existing deferred item as a 2026-dated replication template (post-reopen realized-vol multiple, cross-stock correlation change) than opened as an independent addition. Not independently re-verified beyond the task's own search-indexed-abstract read (SSRN 403'd to direct fetch in both passes).

rejected.name: Systematic Signals of Short Squeezes (Svoboda, Kapounek, Albrecht, 2026)
rejected.reason: Not a new independent gap: mover-v3-sweep-20260924.json already registered Hong-Li-Ni-Scheinkman-Yan's days-to-cover finding on the same short-interest/crowding theme (non_repository_decisions/mover-v3-days-to-cover, 'survives', deferred to v3.1+), with an opposite-signed headline ('high days-to-cover predicts lower returns, no squeeze claim'). The two are not actually contradictory -- one is an unconditional mean-return factor, the other a conditional tail-event-probability claim -- but should be attached to the same registered item with an explicit target-variable split (mean return vs. squeeze-event probability) rather than opened as a separate hypothesis outside the existing preregistration. Not independently re-verified beyond the task's own search-indexed-abstract read (both ScienceDirect and SSRN 5334668 403'd to direct fetch).
